descriptionChirho: Proper masculine name תִּגְלַת פִּלְאֶסֶר / תִּלְּגַת פִּלְנְאֶסֶר: Tiglath-pileser III, king of Assyria (745-727 BCE), one of the most powerful Neo-Assyrian emperors who conquered much of the Levant. The name appears in two orthographic traditions: (1) the Kings tradition תִּגְלַת פִּלְאֶסֶר (2 Kgs 15:29, 16:7, 16:10), closer to the Akkadian Tukulti-apil-Esharra 'my trust is in the son of Esharra,' and (2) the Chronicles tradition תִּלְּגַת פִּלְנְאֶסֶר (1 Chr 5:6, 5:26; 2 Chr 28:20), a variant spelling. Arabic تِغْلَثَ فِلَاسَرَ / تِلكَت فِلنَاسِر (reflecting both traditions), Korean 디글랫 필레세르 / 디글랏 빌레셀, Spanish Tiglat-Pileser / Tilgat-Pilneser, Hindi तिग्लतपिलेसेर / तिल्गत पिल्नेसेर, German Tiglath-Pileser. All five auto-clusters represent the same individual, split because the compound name was tokenized into its two parts in different books.
